Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Player Turn 2.1 Place a piece 2.2 Move a piece 3 Game end 3.1 Draw 3.2 Win 4 Variants Overview Objective Surround the opponent's queen bee. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ 2 player abstract. Players compete to gain control of a hive by surrounding their opponent's queen bee. One player plays the black pieces, the other player plays the white pieces. Play area starts empty. Player Turn Must make a move if possible, otherwise their turn is skipped. Each turn choose to either: Place a new piece. Move a piece. Place a piece Must be on the edge of the hive. Queen bee must be placed in your first 4 turns. After each player has placed their first piece: Must touch a piece of the same color. Cannot touch a piece of the opposite color. Note: Stacks are the color of the top piece. Move a piece You cannot move pieces until your queen bee is placed. Imaginary hexagonal grid. Adjacent pieces always touch a complete edge. All pieces must form one contiguous group at all times ( One Hive rule, see below). A piece cannot move through a gap that is too narrow ( Freedom to Move rule, see below). Queen bee Slides to an adjacent space. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Beetle Slides or climbs to an adjacent space. Cannot be first placed on top of the hive. Any covered pieces cannot be used. Can drop down into any space. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Moving to the ​ space would violate the Freedom to Move rule (see below). Spider Slides 3 spaces around the hive in one direction. When adjacent to more than one part of the hive, it may continue on any side of the hive. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ 1 ​ 1 ​ 2 ​ 2 ​ 2 ​ 2 ​ ​ ​ ​ Soldier Ant Slides anywhere. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Grasshopper Jumps over a line of one or more pieces to the first empty space. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Ladybug Climbs 2 spaces over the hive and 1 space to the edge of the hive. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ 1 ​ 2 ​ 2 ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Pillbug Slides to an adjacent space or moves an adjacent piece to another space adjacent to the pillbug. Cannot move a piece moved in the previous turn. Moved piece cannot move in the next turn. Cannot move a piece in a stack. Pillbug movement ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Pillbug special ability ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Freedom to Move ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Mosquito Copies any adjacent piece. Beetle: remains a beetle until it moves to the edge of the hive. Cannot copy pieces underneath a beetle. Cannot move when only adjacent to the other mosquito. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ One Hive rule All played pieces must be linked at all times. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ cannot move because it would disconnect ​ from the hive, either permanently or temporarily while moving. Freedom to Move rule Cannot move through a narrow gate ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Game end Draw By agreement / repetition. Both queen bees are surrounded on all sides in the same move. Win Only the opponent's queen bee is surrounded on all sides. Variants Expansion pieces: Ladybug Mosquito Pillbug Opening: Standard : no restriction Tournament : The queen bee may not be placed in the first turn. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] The rules are too complicated. Once you learned the rules, you figure out the winning strategy in maybe 10 games. First player always wins. Lock the enemy bee with your ant first so that it can't move, then finish it up with ants or grashoppers.

[Rating: 1/10] Very good chesslike game that seems to inspire even those who don't like chess, although it's not really any more strongly themed or anything.  Definitely worthy of study but easy enough to get into that playing casually is rewarding too.  Since it isn't as mainstream as chess, it also hasn't reached the same level of dedication; lots of general gamers of varying Hive strengths are willing to play, which I can't say has been true of chess in my experience (usually the only ones who want to play chess are chess lifers).

[Rating: 1/10] Guess I'm just not much of an abstract guy.  It's an okay game I'm just not an abstract player.  I prefer card games that are light weight over abstract board games.  It is however an interesting concept and I do like the different moves.  I only wish it wasn't so hard to win.  It feels more like a game of tic-tac-toe meets chess to me.  But that is just my opinion.

[Rating: 1/10] To many draws! Who goes first will win the game or It's a draw.  This game is not good do not buy it!  Save your money!

[Rating: 1/10] Probably a well designed game and my one star rating may be too low, but I hate this game. Players can trap you so it's impossible to move any of your pieces.  Hive is basically Chess with insects and I hate Chess.

[Rating: 1/10] This is chess in a different form. And as much as I respect chess, I don't have the best time playing it.
